findings.title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
findings.body: The original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light branch of `dark-light-choose` uses 70% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). This PR is supposed to only add a dark-theme variant, yet it silently lightens the embedded-post author name in light themes by 40 percentage points, likely producing a near-invisible, low-contrast link. The light branch should remain 30% (dark branch 70%).

findings.title: custom-message-length light color inverted
findings.body: Original: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. New: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` — the light-theme lightness was changed from 70% to 30%, making the hint text much darker than before on light themes (and inconsistent with desktop/modal.scss which kept 70%/30%). Swap the arguments to preserve existing light-theme appearance.

findings.title: topic-map h3 light color changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`; the new light branch uses 50%, lightening the heading noticeably on light themes. The desktop equivalent kept 20%/80%, so mobile and desktop now diverge. Use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name light color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The `.name` rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and now uses 50% in the light branch, reducing contrast on light themes and making `.name` indistinguishable from `.title`. The same regression exists in app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss (`.group-member-info .name`). Keep 30% for the light branch (70% for dark).
